wins.text: Q3 total revenue hit a record $16B, up 22% YoY, with consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $10.7B (67% of revenue), up 30% YoY — both records
AI semiconductor revenue of $5.2B in Q3, up 63% YoY — 10th consecutive quarter of robust growth — with Q4 AI semi revenue guided to $6.2B, up 66% YoY
Secured a fourth XPU customer with over $10B of AI rack orders, expected to ship primarily in Q3 FY2026, materially improving FY2026 AI revenue outlook above prior 50-60% growth trajectory
Infrastructure software operating margin expanded to ~77% from 67% a year ago, reflecting completion of VMware integration; gross margin improved to 93% from 90% YoY
Consolidated backlog hit a record $110B, driven primarily by AI semiconductors, with non-AI semiconductor bookings also up 23% YoY

risks.text: Non-AI semiconductor revenue of $4B was flat sequentially in Q3, with enterprise networking and server storage down sequentially; recovery characterized as U-shaped, with meaningful recovery not expected until mid-to-late FY2026
Q4 consolidated gross margin guided down ~70 bps sequentially due to higher mix of lower-margin XPUs and wireless revenue, with semiconductor gross margins under pressure from product mix
Broadcom explicitly limits its addressable XPU/custom AI market to ~7 identified customers/prospects globally, capping the long-term customer expansion opportunity
Competition in XPU/ASIC space acknowledged, with management noting the need to continuously out-invest and out-innovate rivals to maintain position
VMware VCF deployment (vs. mere licensing) remains a multi-year execution challenge; success with the broader 300K customer base beyond top 10K is uncertain

guidance_items.detail: Q4 FY2025 consolidated revenue guided to ~$17.4B, up 24% YoY, above Q3 actual of $16B
Q4 AI semiconductor revenue guided to ~$6.2B, up 66% YoY; total semiconductor revenue ~$10.7B, up 30% YoY
Q4 infrastructure software revenue guided to ~$6.7B, up 15% YoY, roughly in line with Q3 run rate
Q4 consolidated gross margin expected down ~70 bps sequentially on higher XPU and wireless mix; adjusted EBITDA margin held at 67%
FY2026 AI revenue outlook described as accelerating materially above the prior 50-60% YoY growth rate, driven by fourth customer and continued share gains at existing three customers

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Competitive threats to XPU/ASIC business from U.S. and Asian vendors not proactively addressed
Scale-up Ethernet vs. UALink/PCIe competitive dynamics not discussed in prepared remarks
Gross margin bridge mechanics for Q4 (XPU/wireless mix impact on segment-level margins) not broken out proactively
